---
title: "Cross-Validation Fold Composition"
subtitle: "Reviewer point R2.5: held-out folds of the VAE embedding, thresholds 7 & 8"
---

## Overview

Reviewer 2 (point R2.5) asked how the cross-validation split of the VAE was made. This notebook rebuilds the five folds exactly as `VAE/lite/01_vae_embedding.qmd` does (same input files, same row order, same seed and the same `rsample::vfold_cv()` call), tabulates the held-out composition by fold and dementia group at both thresholds, and shows why stratification on `demcat` balanced only the two largest groups: under the default `pool = 0.1`, `rsample::make_strata()` pools every group forming less than 10% of the sample into the larger strata at random.

No VAE is trained here and no existing output is read for anything but an identity check, so the published embeddings are untouched. The result is quoted in the response letter; no manuscript float reads it.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages

# tidyverse, here and glue are pre-loaded by .Rprofile
pacman::p_load(rsample, install = FALSE)

fmt_count <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
```

## Configuration

The fold settings copied from `01_vae_embedding.qmd`: five folds, seed 123 set immediately before the split, thresholds 7 and 8.

```{r}
#| label: config

N_FOLDS <- 5
SEED <- 123
THRESHOLDS <- c(7, 8)

output_dir <- here("VAE/lite/output")
fs::dir_create(output_dir)
```

## Load data

The covariate-adjusted, scaled methylation matrices that the VAE was trained on, read with the same function body as the embedding notebook so that the row order, and therefore the fold assignment, is the same.

### Input matrices

One matrix per threshold; only `demcat` and the row order enter the split, but the dimensions are checked against those of the training run.

```{r}
#| label: load-data

load_threshold_data <- function(threshold) {
  file_path <- here(glue(
    "data/collaborator_only/adjusted_meth/adjusted_methylation_scaled_nlog10p_gte_{threshold}.rds"
  ))

  data <- read_rds(file_path)

  meth_matrix <- data |>
    select(starts_with("cg")) |>
    as.matrix()

  list(
    matrix = meth_matrix,
    demcat = data$demcat,
    subject_id = data$subject_id,
    n_subjects = nrow(meth_matrix),
    n_features = ncol(meth_matrix),
    threshold = threshold
  )
}

datasets <- map(THRESHOLDS, load_threshold_data) |>
  set_names(glue("threshold_{THRESHOLDS}"))

dataset_dims <- tibble(
  threshold = THRESHOLDS,
  n_subjects = unname(map_int(datasets, "n_subjects")),
  n_features = unname(map_int(datasets, "n_features"))
)

stopifnot(
  all(dataset_dims$n_subjects == 2491),
  identical(dataset_dims$n_features, c(949L, 403L))
)

dataset_dims
```

### Identity check against the saved embeddings

The embedding notebook averages the fold models with `summarise(.by = c(subject_id, demcat))`, which keeps the input row order, so its saved output must list the same participants and groups in the same order as the input read here. The check confirms that this notebook splits the rows the training run split.

```{r}
#| label: check-input

walk(THRESHOLDS, \(threshold) {
  ds <- datasets[[glue("threshold_{threshold}")]]
  embedding <- read_rds(here(output_dir, glue("embedding_threshold_{threshold}.rds")))

  stopifnot(
    identical(as.character(embedding$subject_id), as.character(ds$subject_id)),
    identical(as.character(embedding$demcat), as.character(ds$demcat)),
    is.factor(ds$demcat),
    !anyNA(ds$demcat)
  )
})

stopifnot(identical(datasets$threshold_7$subject_id, datasets$threshold_8$subject_id))
stopifnot(identical(datasets$threshold_7$demcat, datasets$threshold_8$demcat))

levels(datasets$threshold_8$demcat)
```

Both inputs hold the same `r fmt_count(dataset_dims$n_subjects[1])` participants in the same order, matching the saved embeddings row for row.

## Rebuild the folds

The split is rebuilt with the embedding notebook's own call: `set.seed(123)` immediately before `vfold_cv()` on a two-column tibble of row index and `demcat`. Nothing else draws random numbers in between, so the earlier seeds and the TensorFlow seeds of that notebook do not affect the split.

```{r}
#| label: rebuild-folds

rebuild_folds <- function(data) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  cv_splits <- vfold_cv(
    tibble(idx = 1:nrow(data$matrix), demcat = data$demcat),
    v = N_FOLDS,
    strata = demcat
  )

  map(seq_len(N_FOLDS), \(fold_idx) {
    fold_split <- cv_splits$splits[[fold_idx]]
    train_idx <- as.integer(fold_split, data = "analysis")
    test_idx <- as.integer(fold_split, data = "assessment")

    stopifnot(length(intersect(train_idx, test_idx)) == 0)

    tibble(
      idx = test_idx,
      subject_id = data$subject_id[test_idx],
      demcat = data$demcat[test_idx],
      fold = fold_idx,
      n_train = length(train_idx)
    )
  }) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(threshold = data$threshold, .before = 1)
}

fold_assignment <- map(datasets, rebuild_folds) |>
  list_rbind()

# Every participant is held out exactly once at each threshold
stopifnot(
  fold_assignment |>
    count(threshold, idx) |>
    pull(n) |>
    (\(n) all(n == 1))(),
  all(count(fold_assignment, threshold)$n == 2491)
)

# The two thresholds share row order and demcat, so the folds must coincide
folds_identical <- identical(
  fold_assignment |> dplyr::filter(threshold == 7) |> arrange(idx) |> pull(fold),
  fold_assignment |> dplyr::filter(threshold == 8) |> arrange(idx) |> pull(fold)
)

stopifnot(folds_identical)
```

The fold assignment is `r if (folds_identical) "identical" else "different"` at thresholds 7 and 8, as expected: the split depends only on the row order and `demcat`, not on the CpG columns.

## Held-out composition

Counts of each dementia group in each held-out fold, with the training size of the corresponding model. The last two rows give the group totals and the exact 20% share a perfectly stratified fold would hold.

### Counts per fold and group

Long-format counts at both thresholds; `.drop = FALSE` keeps a zero for any group absent from a fold.

```{r}
#| label: composition-long

composition_long <- fold_assignment |>
  count(threshold, fold, n_train, demcat, .drop = FALSE, name = "n_heldout")

composition_long
```

### Composition table

One row per held-out fold. The table is printed once, because the two thresholds give the same folds.

```{r}
#| label: composition-table

group_levels <- levels(datasets$threshold_8$demcat)

fold_rows <- composition_long |>
  dplyr::filter(threshold == 8) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = demcat, values_from = n_heldout) |>
  mutate(
    n_heldout = rowSums(pick(all_of(group_levels)), na.rm = TRUE),
    .after = n_train
  ) |>
  transmute(
    row = as.character(fold),
    n_train = as.numeric(n_train),
    n_heldout = as.numeric(n_heldout),
    across(all_of(group_levels), as.numeric)
  )

group_totals <- fold_rows |>
  summarise(across(c(n_heldout, all_of(group_levels)), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  mutate(row = "Group total", n_train = NA_real_)

exact_share <- group_totals |>
  mutate(
    across(c(n_heldout, all_of(group_levels)), \(x) x / N_FOLDS),
    row = "Exact 20% share"
  )

composition_table <- bind_rows(fold_rows, group_totals, exact_share) |>
  relocate(row, n_train, n_heldout)

stopifnot(group_totals$n_heldout == 2491)

composition_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Held-out fold", "Training n", "Held-out n", group_levels),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )
```

### Range across folds

The smallest and largest held-out count of each group across the five folds, as quoted in the response to R2.5.

```{r}
#| label: group-ranges

group_ranges <- composition_long |>
  dplyr::filter(threshold == 8) |>
  summarise(
    n_total = sum(n_heldout, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_heldout = min(n_heldout, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_heldout = max(n_heldout, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = demcat
  )

size_ranges <- fold_rows |>
  summarise(
    min_train = min(n_train, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_train = max(n_train, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_heldout = min(n_heldout, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_heldout = max(n_heldout, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

group_ranges

size_ranges
```

Training sets held `r fmt_count(size_ranges$min_train)`–`r fmt_count(size_ranges$max_train)` participants and held-out folds `r size_ranges$min_heldout`–`r size_ranges$max_heldout`.

## Pooling rule

Why stratification on `demcat` balanced only two groups. The rule is read from the installed rsample, not restated from its documentation.

### Default pool and the make_strata source

`vfold_cv()` passes `pool` to `make_strata()` unchanged; the embedding notebook does not set it, so the default applies. The source lines below are the ones that pool small groups: any level whose share of the sample is below `pool` is set to missing, and the missing entries are then drawn at random from the remaining levels.

```{r}
#| label: pool-rule

rsample_version <- as.character(packageVersion("rsample"))
default_pool <- eval(formals(rsample::vfold_cv)$pool)

stopifnot(identical(eval(formals(rsample::make_strata)$pool), default_pool))

make_strata_source <- deparse(body(rsample::make_strata))
pooling_lines <- make_strata_source[
  str_detect(make_strata_source, "pcts < pool|sample\\(levels\\(out\\)|out\\[is.na\\(x\\)\\]|num_miss <- ")
] |>
  str_trim()

pooling_lines
```

With rsample `r rsample_version`, the default is pool = `r default_pool`.

### Group shares

Each group's share of the 2,491 participants, and whether it falls under the pool threshold.

```{r}
#| label: group-shares

group_shares <- tibble(demcat = datasets$threshold_8$demcat) |>
  count(demcat, name = "n") |>
  mutate(
    share = n / sum(n, na.rm = TRUE),
    pooled = share < default_pool
  )

pooled_groups <- group_shares |>
  dplyr::filter(pooled) |>
  pull(demcat) |>
  as.character()

kept_groups <- group_shares |>
  dplyr::filter(!pooled) |>
  pull(demcat) |>
  as.character()

stopifnot(
  setequal(kept_groups, c("stable_normal", "normal2incid")),
  length(pooled_groups) == 4
)

group_shares
```

The four groups below 10% (`r paste(pooled_groups, collapse = ", ")`) were pooled; only `r paste(kept_groups, collapse = " and ")` formed strata.

### Strata actually used

`vfold_cv()` calls `make_strata()` as its first random draw, so the same seed reproduces the strata it used. Each pooled participant ends up in one of the two remaining strata; within each stratum the folds are then assigned evenly, so every stratum must differ by at most one participant across folds, which confirms the reconstruction.

```{r}
#| label: strata-used

set.seed(SEED)
strata_used <- make_strata(datasets$threshold_8$demcat, pool = default_pool)

strata_by_group <- tibble(
  stratum = strata_used,
  demcat = datasets$threshold_8$demcat
) |>
  count(stratum, demcat, .drop = FALSE, name = "n") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stratum, values_from = n)

strata_by_fold <- tibble(
  idx = seq_along(strata_used),
  stratum = strata_used
) |>
  left_join(
    fold_assignment |> dplyr::filter(threshold == 8) |> select(idx, fold),
    by = "idx"
  ) |>
  count(stratum, fold, name = "n") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = fold, values_from = n, names_prefix = "fold_")

stratum_spread <- strata_by_fold |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(spread = diff(range(c_across(starts_with("fold_")), na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  ungroup()

stopifnot(
  setequal(levels(strata_used), kept_groups),
  all(stratum_spread$spread <= 1)
)

strata_by_group

strata_by_fold
```

Every pooled participant was placed in the stable_normal or normal2incid stratum, and each stratum is split evenly across the five folds (spread at most one). The groups themselves are therefore balanced only to the extent that their randomly allocated members happen to fall evenly.

## Save

The fold composition, the per-group ranges and the pooling evidence, with the settings that produced them.

```{r}
#| label: save

cv_fold_composition <- list(
  composition_long = composition_long,
  composition_table = composition_table,
  group_ranges = group_ranges,
  size_ranges = size_ranges,
  group_shares = group_shares,
  strata_by_group = strata_by_group,
  strata_by_fold = strata_by_fold,
  folds_identical_across_thresholds = folds_identical,
  settings = list(
    seed = SEED,
    v = N_FOLDS,
    strata = "demcat",
    pool = default_pool,
    rsample_version = rsample_version,
    thresholds = THRESHOLDS
  )
)

write_rds(cv_fold_composition, here(output_dir, "cv_fold_composition.rds"))
```
